proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  By consistency, on the event \(A=a\) one has \(Y=Y(a)\), and by conditional ignorability,
\[
 \mathbb E_Q\{Y(a)\mid A=a,X\}=\mathbb E_Q\{Y(a)\mid X\}
 \qquad Q\text{-almost surely},\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Overlap makes both treatment strata nonnull conditionally on \(X=x\).  Consequently, for \(Q_X\)-almost every \(x\),
\[
 \mu_{a,Q}(x)=\mathbb E_Q\{Y(a)\mid X=x\},
 \qquad
 \tau_Q(x)=\mathbb E_Q\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}.
\]
The functions \(\mu_{0,Q}\) and \(\tau_Q\) are continuous by the two stated H\"older assumptions, and hence \(\mu_{1,Q}=\mu_{0,Q}+\tau_Q\) is continuous.  The right-hand side in the second display therefore has the continuous version \(\tau_Q\).

It remains to justify evaluation at a point.  If two continuous versions \(g_1,g_2\) on \(x_0+[-r_0,r_0]^d\) agree \(Q_X\)-almost everywhere but differ at some point \(x\), continuity supplies a relatively open ball \(U\) on which \(|g_1-g_2|>0\).  This set has positive Lebesgue measure.  The local density lower bound then gives
\[
 Q_X(U)=\int_U f_Q(u)\,du\ge \underline f\,\operatorname{Leb}(U)>0,
\]
contradicting almost-everywhere equality.  Thus the continuous versions are unique throughout the anchor neighborhood.  Evaluating the preceding equality at \(x_0\) proves
\[
 \tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)=\tau_Q(x_0)
 =\mu_{1,Q}(x_0)-\mu_{0,Q}(x_0).
\]

Let \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  Every defining condition of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), except the two density inequalities, is already a defining condition of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  Uniform design gives \(f_Q=1\) Lebesgue-almost everywhere.  Since \(\underline f\le1\le\overline f\),
\[
 f_Q(x)\le\overline f\quad\text{on }\mathcal X,
 \qquad
 f_Q(x)\ge\underline f\quad\text{on }x_0+[-r_0,r_0]^d
\]
up to Lebesgue-null sets.  Hence \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), proving \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\subset\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).

Write \(\ell=h k^{-1/d}\).  Because \(1\le k\le m h^d\),
\[
 m^{-1/d}\le \ell\le h\le r_0\le\frac14.
\]
The definitions, \(m\asymp n\), and \(\sqrt{a+b}\le\sqrt a+\sqrt b\) give, with constants depending only on the displayed fixed quantities and \(\eta\),
\[
\begin{split}
 B(h,k)&\lesssim h^\gamma+\ell^q,\\
 S(h,k,\eta)&\lesssim n^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}
       +n^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2},\\
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)&\lesssim
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-d}
       +N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-d}\ell^{-d}.
\end{split}
\]
Indeed, \(h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\le h^\gamma\), \(\sqrt{k}=h^{d/2}\ell^{-d/2}\), and \(k h^{-2d}=h^{-d}\ell^{-d}\).  The two logarithms in the definition of \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}\) differ from those in \(G\) only by a factor depending on the fixed \(\eta\).

Let
\[
 r_o=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},\qquad
 r_2=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q))}.
\]
Direct comparison of their exponents at
\(q=d/\{2(1+d/(2\gamma))\}\) shows that
\(r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_o\vee r_2\).  Put
\(t=r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}}\), with the corrected \(r_{\mathrm{ho}}\).

First suppose \(q<\gamma\) and \(t\) is smaller than a fixed constant.  Choose, up to fixed multiplicative constants,
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad \ell=t^{1/q},\qquad
 k=(h/\ell)^d,
\]
rounding \(k\) to a positive integer.  Integer rounding changes every displayed order only by a fixed factor.  The inequalities \(t\ge r_o,r_2,r_{\mathrm{reg}},r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) are respectively equivalent to
\[
 n^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}\le t,
 \quad n^{-1}t^{-d/(2\gamma)-d/(2q)}\le t,
 \quad N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma}\le t,
 \quad N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma-d/q}\le t.
\]
They bound all four fluctuation terms, while \(h^\gamma=\ell^q=t\).

The rank restriction also holds for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Indeed, \(\epsilon_n\le1\), \(\delta_n<1/2\), and \(\eta<1/4\) imply \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}\le C_\eta n\).  If
\(a_{\mathrm{ho}}=1/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)\), then
\(a_{\mathrm{ho}}\le q/d\).  Hence \(t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}\gtrsim n^{-q/d}\), so \(\ell=t^{1/q}\gtrsim n^{-1/d}\), which is equivalent, up to the harmless factor between \(m\) and \(n\), to \(k\le m h^d\).  Also \(m h^d\to\infty\), so the stated local-sample constraint eventually holds.

If \(q\ge\gamma\), take \(k=1\), so \(\ell=h\), and take \(h=t^{1/\gamma}\).  Then \(\ell^q\le h^\gamma=t\).  The first sampling term is bounded because \(t\ge r_o\), and the second is its square and is therefore no larger for sufficiently large \(n\).  The leading privacy term is now
\(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-2d}\); the corrected formula gives
\(r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+2d/\gamma)}\), so this term is at most \(t\).  The remaining privacy term is smaller.  This also proves why replacing \(q\) by \(\bar q=\min\{q,\gamma\}\) is necessary.

If \(t\) is bounded below by a fixed constant, any feasible choice suffices because \(C_n(h,k)\subset[-1,1]\) and hence its length is at most two.  For \(n\ge n_0\), the feasible set is nonempty and compact after restricting \(h\) by the displayed local-sample inequality; since \(k\) ranges over finitely many integers, a minimizer exists.  Its radius is no larger than the radius at the preceding candidate.  Finally,
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(h,k)\}\le 2R_n(h,k)
\]
deterministically.  Taking expectations and the supremum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) proves the result.  The proof concerns length only and does not use the unresolved stochastic-remainder assertion.

Again put \(\ell=h k^{-1/d}\).  The constraint \(k\le m h^d\) gives \(\ell\ge m^{-1/d}\), and therefore every admissible choice obeys
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)\gtrsim \ell^q\gtrsim n^{-q/d}.
\]
The same objective also dominates
\[
 h^\gamma+n^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}
\]
and hence its infimum is at least
\(r_o=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\).  Finally it dominates, up to fixed factors,
\[
 h^\gamma+\ell^q+n^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2}.
\]
If all three summands were smaller than \(t\), then
\(h<t^{1/\gamma}\), \(\ell<t^{1/q}\), and the last summand would exceed
\(n^{-1}t^{-d/(2\gamma)-d/(2q)}\).  Balancing this expression with \(t\) proves the lower bound
\[
 r_2=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q))}.
\]
The elbow in the definition of \(r_{\mathrm{np}}\) is exactly the solution of \(r_o=r_2\), so \(r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_o\vee r_2\).  This proves the asserted lower bound.

For the reverse inequality set
\(T=r_o\vee r_2\vee n^{-q/d}\).  If \(q<\gamma\), take
\(h=T^{1/\gamma}\), \(\ell=T^{1/q}\), and round
\(k=(h/\ell)^d\) to a positive integer.  The term \(n^{-q/d}\) ensures \(\ell\gtrsim m^{-1/d}\), hence \(k\le m h^d\), and \(r_o,r_2\le T\) give
\[
 n^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}\le T,
 \qquad
 n^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2}\le T.
\]
The two leading biases equal \(T\), while
\(h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\le h^\gamma=T\).  If \(q\ge\gamma\), take \(k=1\) and \(h=T^{1/\gamma}\); then \(h^q\le h^\gamma=T\), and the second sampling term is the square of the first and is smaller for large \(n\).  In both cases the local-sample and boundary constraints hold for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Integer rounding and \(m\asymp n\) alter only constants.  This proves the matching upper bound and the claimed characterization.

Choose a nonnegative \(C^\infty\) function \(\varphi\), supported on \([-1,1]^d\), with \(\varphi(0)=1\).  Put
\(p_* = \min\{1/4,L_\mu/2\}>0\).  Choose a constant \(a_*>0\), depending only on \((L_\tau,p_*,\gamma,d)\), so small that for every \(0<h\le r_0\),
\[
 g_h(x)=a_*h^\gamma\varphi((x-x_0)/h)
\]
belongs to \(\mathcal H^\gamma(L_\tau;\mathcal X)\) and obeys \(0\le g_h\le p_*/2\).  This is possible because each derivative of order \(j\le\lfloor\gamma\rfloor\) scales as \(a_*h^{\gamma-j}\), while the top-order H\"older seminorm is bounded by a constant times \(a_*\).  The support lies in \(\mathcal X\) by the boundary and bandwidth conditions.

Define two full-data laws \(Q_0,Q_h\) as follows.  Under both, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal X\), \(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and \(A\) is conditionally independent of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \(X\).  Under \(Q_0\), conditional on \(X\), take \(Y(0),Y(1)\) independent Bernoulli variables of mean \(p_*\).  Under \(Q_h\), use respective means \(p_*\) and \(p_*+g_h(X)\).  In both laws set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  These laws have common support \(\{0,1\}\), satisfy consistency and ignorability by construction, satisfy overlap because \(\kappa<1/2\), and satisfy both density bounds because \(\underline f\le1\le\overline f\).  The constant propensity belongs to its H\"older ball by \(L_\pi\ge1/2\); the constant control regression belongs to its ball by the choice of \(p_*\); and the CATEs are \(0\) and \(g_h\).  Hence \(Q_0,Q_h\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\subset\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Their causal target separation is
\[
 \Delta_h=|\tau_{Q_h}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)-\tau_{Q_0}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)|=a_*h^\gamma.
\]

Let \(P_0,P_h\) be the corresponding one-record observed laws.  A direct calculation in the treated Bernoulli stratum gives
\[
 \chi^2(P_h\|P_0)
 =\frac12\int_{\mathcal X}\frac{g_h(x)^2}{p_*(1-p_*)}\,dx
 \le C_\chi h^{2\gamma+d},
\]
and
\[
 \|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12\int_{\mathcal X}g_h(x)\,dx
 \le C_v h^{\gamma+d}.
\]
Both constants are fixed and finite because \(p_*\in(0,1/2)\) and \(\varphi\) is bounded with compact support.

For the privacy-free part, likelihood factorization and Fubini give the exact product identity
\[
 1+\chi^2(P_h^n\|P_0^n)=\{1+\chi^2(P_h\|P_0)\}^n.
\]
Also, Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the product likelihood ratio \(L\) gives
\[
 \|P_h^n-P_0^n\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{P_0^n}|L-1|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(P_h^n\|P_0^n)}.
\]
Taking \(h=c_1n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)}\), with \(c_1\le r_0\) sufficiently small, makes the last total variation at most \(1/8\).  Passing the sample through any randomized interval mechanism cannot increase total variation, since for every output event the difference is an integral of a function taking values in \([0,1]\).

For the privacy part, take
\[
 h=c_2\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-1}\}^{1/(\gamma+d)},
\]
where \(c_2\le r_0\) is chosen so that
\(\|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le a_0\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-1}\}\) and
\(a_0(e-1+c_0)\le1/8\).  The Hamming-transport lemma, \(e^u-1\le(e-1)u\) for \(0\le u\le1\), and \(n\delta_n\le c_0\) imply
\[
 \|P_h^n\mathsf K-P_0^n\mathsf K\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le n\|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
       (e^{\epsilon_n}-1+\delta_n)
 \le a_0(e-1+c_0)\le\frac18,
\]
where \(\mathsf K\) denotes the interval-release kernel.

It remains to turn either indistinguishable pair into a length bound.  Let \(\nu_j\) denote the two output laws, let \(\theta_j\) be their target values, and set \(E_j=\{\theta_j\in\widetilde C_n\}\).  Honesty gives \(\nu_j(E_j)\ge1-\eta\).  If \(\|\nu_0-\nu_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1/8\), then
\[
 \nu_0(E_0\cap E_1)
 \ge \nu_0(E_0)+\nu_0(E_1)-1
 \ge 1-2\eta-\frac18>\frac38.
\]
On this intersection the interval has length at least \(|\theta_1-\theta_0|=\Delta_h\).  Therefore its expected length under \(Q_0\) is at least \(3\Delta_h/8\).  The first bandwidth gives the term \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), and the second gives
\(1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\).  Applying the two conclusions separately to the same arbitrary mechanism and taking the smaller of their fixed constants proves the maximum of the two terms.

The truncation by one is necessary: the deterministic interval \([-1,1]\) is private, honest, and has length two, so the untruncated expression in the frozen statement cannot hold uniformly as \(n\epsilon_n\downarrow0\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathsf K\) be any replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private Markov kernel from samples of size \(n\) in a standard Borel record space to an arbitrary output space.  If \(\Lambda_0\) and \(\Lambda_1\) are any two laws on the sample space and \(H(z,z')\) is Hamming distance, then their output laws \(\nu_j=\Lambda_j\mathsf K\) satisfy
\[
 \|\nu_0-\nu_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \min\!\left\{1,\bigl(e^{\epsilon_n}-1+\delta_n\bigr)
 \inf_{\Gamma\in\Pi(\Lambda_0,\Lambda_1)}\mathbb E_\Gamma H(Z,Z')\right\}.
\]
In particular, for one-record laws \(R_0,R_1\),
\[
 \|R_0^n\mathsf K-R_1^n\mathsf K\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \min\{1,n\|R_0-R_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}(e^{\epsilon_n}-1+\delta_n)\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(c_{\mathrm{DP}}=e^{\epsilon_n}-1+\delta_n\).  If \(z,z'\) are replacement adjacent and \(E\) is an output event, differential privacy in both directions gives
\[
 \mathsf K_z(E)-\mathsf K_{z'}(E)
 \le (e^{\epsilon_n}-1)\mathsf K_{z'}(E)+\delta_n
 \le c_{\mathrm{DP}},
\]
and the same inequality with \(z,z'\) interchanged.  Hence
\(\|\mathsf K_z-\mathsf K_{z'}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le c_{\mathrm{DP}}\).
Joining arbitrary \(z,z'\) by a path that replaces precisely their \(H(z,z')\) unequal coordinates and using the triangle inequality yields
\[
 \|\mathsf K_z-\mathsf K_{z'}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le c_{\mathrm{DP}}H(z,z').
\]
For any coupling \(\Gamma\in\Pi(\Lambda_0,\Lambda_1)\) and any output event \(E\),
\[
 |\nu_0(E)-\nu_1(E)|
 \le\int |\mathsf K_z(E)-\mathsf K_{z'}(E)|\,d\Gamma(z,z')
 \le c_{\mathrm{DP}}\mathbb E_\Gamma H(Z,Z').
\]
Taking the supremum over \(E\), then the infimum over \(\Gamma\), and finally using the trivial upper bound one proves the first display.  For product laws, couple the coordinates independently using the common-part coupling of \(R_0\) and \(R_1\).  Its mismatch probability is \(\|R_0-R_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), so its expected Hamming distance is \(n\|R_0-R_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), which proves the second display.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
The concrete attainable model satisfies \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\subset\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  In particular, for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), its uniform design obeys
\[
 \underline f\le f_Q(x)\le\overline f
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X\), including throughout the anchor neighborhood.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The class inclusion and density implications follow directly from uniform design.  The additional Gram assertion is not well typed: the frozen core defines neither the localized Gram matrices, their weights, nor the normalization of the Legendre basis.  Removing that clause is necessary rather than importing an unstated normalization.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
There are constants \(n_0\in\mathbb N\) and \(C_L<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\), such that, for \(n\ge n_0\), choose \((h,k)\) by deterministic minimization of \(B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\) over \(h\le r_0\), \(1\le k\le m h^d\), and \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\).  For any deterministic pilot spline dimensions \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\),
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}\{C_n(h,k)\}]
 \le C_L r_{\mathrm{up}},
\]
where \(r_{\mathrm{up}}\) uses \(\bar q=\min\{q,\gamma\}\) as in the corrected phase-rate definition.  Thus the length of this global-sensitivity construction is governed by the privacy-free term, the ordinary private-regression term, and a higher-order term which equals the \(q\)-branch for \(q<\gamma\) and the private-Gram branch \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}\) for \(q\ge\gamma\).  No matching full-class lower claim is made.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim quantifies without ensuring that the tuning set is nonempty.  Moreover, feasibility \(k\ge1\) forces the higher-order privacy branch to saturate at \(q=\gamma\).  The proposed claim adds the necessary large-sample qualification and states the phase corresponding to the corrected rate definition; it does not strengthen the model class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
With the Gaussian release noises set to zero and the privacy constraint removed, the constrained optimization actually satisfies, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \inf_{\substack{h\le r_0,\ 1\le k\le m h^d\\
                  m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)}}
 \{B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)\}
 \asymp r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee n^{-q/d}.
\]
Thus it equals the advertised KBRW rate precisely in the regimes in which \(r_{\mathrm{np}}\gtrsim n^{-q/d}\); in the low-smoothness regime where the reverse inequality holds, the frozen rank cap forces the additional approximation floor \(n^{-q/d}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The imposed constraint \(k\le m h^d\) implies \(h k^{-1/d}\ge m^{-1/d}\), so the nuisance bias is at least a constant times \(n^{-q/d}\).  In the low-smoothness KBRW regime the unconstrained KBRW tuning violates this rank cap, making the frozen equality false on the unchanged attainable class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume \(L_\pi\ge1/2\).  Let \(\widetilde C_n\) be any replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private interval satisfying
\[
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}}
 \Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in\widetilde C_n\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
If \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), then
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}(\widetilde C_n)]
 \ge c\left[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \vee\left\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\right\}\right].
\]
The constant \(c>0\) depends only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\).  The lower bound uses a randomized-treatment, uniform-design, strictly positive regression submodel and contains no \(q<\gamma\) paired-cell branch.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The untruncated privacy term diverges when \(n\epsilon_n\) tends to zero, whereas the deterministic interval \([-1,1]\) is private, honest, and has length two.  A compatibility condition \(L_\pi\ge1/2\) is also needed for the explicitly claimed randomized-treatment submodel to belong to the stated H\"older ball.  The correction saturates the rate and surfaces that nonemptiness condition without changing the class.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: \(r_{\mathrm{np}}=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s))}\) if \(s<\frac{d/4}{1+d/(2\gamma)}\), and \(r_{\mathrm{np}}=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\) otherwise.  Put \(\bar q=\min\{q,\gamma\}\), \(r_{\mathrm{reg}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\), \(r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\bar q\gamma/\{(d+\bar q)\gamma+\bar q d\}}\), and \(r_{\mathrm{up}}=r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}}\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Writing \(\ell=h k^{-1/d}\) turns the second privacy term into \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-d}\ell^{-d}\), while \(k\ge1\) forces \(\ell\le h\).  For \(q>\gamma\) the frozen optimizer would require \(\ell=t^{1/q}>h\) and is infeasible; the boundary \(k=1\) instead balances \(h^\gamma\) with \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-2d}\), giving exponent \(\gamma/(\gamma+2d)\).  Replacing \(q\) by \(\min\{q,\gamma\}\) in the constructed higher-order phase is the exact feasibility correction.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the claimed joint main-block sensitivity and Gaussian calibration for the concrete higher-order learner.
open_obligations.obstruction: The learner is specified only by reference to all clipped linear and order-two KBRW moment entries.  No kernel formulas, normalizations, clipping radii, pilot release scales, or Gaussian covariance are defined, so replacement sensitivity and approximate-DP calibration are not mathematically determined.
open_obligations.attempted: I verified the parallel-composition and post-processing ledger and rewrote a generic replacement path argument.  Those steps do not determine the sensitivity of an undefined concatenated vector.
open_obligations.partial_result: Parallel composition across the three deterministic disjoint blocks would give overall \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-privacy once each block release were shown to have that guarantee, and all projections, spectral clipping, inversion, and interval formation would then be post-processing.  What cannot be derived is the claimed main-block sensitivity: the construction never defines the linear kernel, the order-two kernel, the normalization of their concatenation, the clipping radii, or the Gaussian covariance.  Those quantities determine whether the joint \(\ell_2\)-sensitivity is \(m^{-1}(h^{-d}+kh^{-2d})\), a square-root-dimensional variant, or another order.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish the finite-sample bias, degenerate-U-statistic fluctuation, and propagated Gaussian-noise bounds for an explicit estimator.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen construction contains no equations for \(\widehat Q\), \(\widehat R\), the quadratic kernel, pilot clipping, or noise scales.  The displayed \(B\), \(S\), and \(G\) envelopes name desired bounds but cannot serve as premises proving them.
open_obligations.attempted: I decomposed the envelopes into localization, cell approximation, linear fluctuation, quadratic fluctuation, and two privacy terms.  This verifies their tuning algebra but cannot verify that the unspecified random estimator has those remainders.
open_obligations.partial_result: If an explicit estimator satisfied the claimed deterministic bias bound and the two claimed stochastic bounds, their union would immediately give the displayed probability inequality.  The present construction does not specify the random variables to which concentration is to be applied.  In particular, no equation defines \(\widehat Q\), \(\widehat R\), the quadratic correction, pilot clipping, or Gaussian scales, so neither the degenerate \(U\)-statistic variance nor propagation through the stabilized inverse can be checked.  The algebraic envelope alone is not a proof of such properties.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Deduce unconditional honest coverage and privacy after proving the two load-bearing release and remainder lemmas.
open_obligations.obstruction: The theorem depends essentially on both unresolved lemmas; treating their conclusions as assumptions would assume the crux.
open_obligations.attempted: The deterministic coverage reduction from identification and the radius definition is complete, but the probability and privacy premises are unavailable.
open_obligations.partial_result: Conditional on the two unresolved lemmas, the result is immediate: the remainder event has probability at least \(1-\eta\), pointwise identification replaces \(\tau_Q(x_0)\) by \(\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\), and the definition of \(C_n(h,k)\) then gives coverage; privacy follows from the release lemma and post-processing.  Since both load-bearing premises remain unproved from the current learner definition, this conditional reduction does not establish the theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine whether a paired-microcell fuzzy family admits an \(n\)-sample coupling with sufficiently small expected Hamming cost, and construct a fully specified private stabilized higher-order estimator over the full unknown-density class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The one-cell identity cancels the one-observation prior mixture but does not control dependencies caused by repeat visits to a latent microcell.  On the upper side, no explicit private Gram/PTR construction is present and the current learner uses known uniform design only.
open_obligations.attempted: I proved the general approximate-DP Hamming-transport inequality, embedded a strictly positive common-support ordinary bump submodel, audited the paired-cell cancellation, and optimized every frozen envelope.  The missing coupling cost and private full-class Gram analysis are precisely the two steps needed to decide the \(q\)-branch.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved ordinary two-law submodel yields the corrected full-class lower bound
\[
 n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee
 \{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}.
\]
The constrained envelope optimization yields, only for the attainable uniform-design construction and subject to the unresolved remainder, the corrected upper phase
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/\min\{q,\gamma\})}.
\]
The Hamming-transport lemma reduces any fuzzy paired-cell privacy lower bound to an explicit coupling-cost calculation.  The identity
\(uv+(1/4-u^2)t=0\) verifies a one-observation prior-mixture cancellation, but it does not by itself construct a coupling of the two \(n\)-sample mixture laws with the required expected Hamming cost; repeated observations from the same latent microcell create dependence.  Nor does the frozen learner specify a propose-test-release or private-Gram algorithm on the full, unknown-design-density class.  Consequently these results give an honest bracket but do not decide whether the nuisance-driven privacy term is minimax unavoidable.
